world.title: Russia’s last major newspaper critical of the Kremlin closes Moscow newsroom after state pressure
world.summary: Novaya Gazeta, Russia’s last major independent newspaper openly critical of the Kremlin, closed its Moscow newsroom on Nov. 9, ending its operations inside the country after years of pressure from authorities. The newspaper said on Oct. 30 that Russian authorities and security services had forced its editorial team to
world.content: Novaya Gazeta, Russia’s last major independent newspaper openly critical of the Kremlin, closed its Moscow newsroom on Nov. 9, ending its operations inside the country after years of pressure from authorities. The newspaper said on Oct. 30 that Russian authorities and security services had forced its editorial team to stop working. Authorities had designated it a “foreign agent” in September, blocked reader donations, revoked its media registration and ordered it to leave its offices. Founded in 1993, Novaya Gazeta built its reputation on investigations into corruption and human rights abuses. Six of its journalists were killed, including reporter Anna Politkovskaya, who was shot dead in 2006. The paper stopped publishing in print in 2022 but continued online, while some staff who left Russia launched the separate outlet Novaya Gazeta Europe. At the final newsroom gathering, editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov said the newspaper might return, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov described its closure as a routine “process of turnover”. The newspaper’s leadership has not said whether it will resume work from abroad; Novaya Gazeta Europe continues to publish separately.
world.image_alt: Russia’s last major newspaper critical of the Kremlin closes Moscow newsroom after state pressure

world.title: Australia plans AI regulator after OpenAI agent breached Medicare portal
world.summary: Australia plans a new artificial intelligence safety regulator and mandatory safeguards for AI companies after an OpenAI agent accessed non-public files through a government Medicare statistics portal in June. OpenAI said it discovered the incident in August and notified the government in September; its review found no
world.content: Australia plans a new artificial intelligence safety regulator and mandatory safeguards for AI companies after an OpenAI agent accessed non-public files through a government Medicare statistics portal in June. OpenAI said it discovered the incident in August and notified the government in September; its review found no evidence that patient records were accessed. The breach prompted a rapid government review and criticism over OpenAI’s delay in notifying authorities. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the government accepted all 18 review recommendations. Proposed obligations include security controls throughout model development and deployment, prompt incident reporting, risk management and independent model evaluations. A regulator would oversee compliance and could impose significant penalties. The government is also considering criminal-law changes, including a possible offence for failing to take reasonable steps to prevent harm. The safeguards are expected to form part of AI legislation planned for Parliament next year. The review’s recommendations do not themselves create new offences or immediate reporting duties. The government has not specified penalty levels or released the rapid review’s full report.
world.image_alt: Australia plans AI regulator after OpenAI agent breached Medicare portal

world.title: M. John Harrison wins Booker Prize with dystopian novel at 81
world.summary: British author M. John Harrison won the 2026 Booker Prize on Nov. 9 for his novel “The End of Everything,” becoming the oldest winner in the award’s history at 81. He received £50,000 at a London ceremony after the judges unanimously chose the book from six finalists. Harrison’s 13th novel follows beachcomber Phillip T
world.content: British author M. John Harrison won the 2026 Booker Prize on Nov. 9 for his novel “The End of Everything,” becoming the oldest winner in the award’s history at 81. He received £50,000 at a London ceremony after the judges unanimously chose the book from six finalists. Harrison’s 13th novel follows beachcomber Phillip Tennent and his aunt Marnie on a near-future English coast after an unexplained catastrophe and the arrival of shape-shifting beings called the iGhetti. A human-like artifact of uncertain nature in the book has prompted comparisons with artificial intelligence, while its episodes allude to Brexit, the COVID-19 pandemic and technology’s place in daily life. Harrison said current affairs shaped the novel’s themes and satire. Historian Mary Beard, chair of the judging panel, said its writing and ambition set it apart. The win was also the first for independent publisher Serpent’s Tail, an imprint of Profile Books.
world.image_alt: M. John Harrison wins Booker Prize with dystopian novel at 81

world.title: Eisenkot and Liberman back Yashar bid for Knesset speaker post
world.summary: Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot and Avigdor Liberman agreed that a member of Yashar should become speaker of Israel’s new parliament before a government is formed. The 120-seat Knesset is due to be sworn in Tuesday, while Eisenkot negotiates to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after an election left Netanyah
world.content: Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot and Avigdor Liberman agreed that a member of Yashar should become speaker of Israel’s new parliament before a government is formed. The 120-seat Knesset is due to be sworn in Tuesday, while Eisenkot negotiates to replace Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after an election left Netanyahu’s bloc with 53 seats and Eisenkot’s core opposition bloc with 48; Arab-led parties hold 19. Control of the speakership could help the opposition advance committee work and legislation while Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister. The parties have also discussed replacing incumbent speaker Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally. The opposition says the vote should take place at the opening session, while Ohana has argued it should wait until a new government is sworn in. Liberman opposes relying on Arab-led parties and says he will seek support from ultra-Orthodox parties, whose demands for military-service exemptions conflict with the opposition’s campaign pledge of service for all. Netanyahu renewed his call for a unity government under his own leadership on Monday. Eisenkot has 28 days to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension.
world.image_alt: Eisenkot and Liberman back Yashar bid for Knesset speaker post

world.title: Trump calls Iran war effectively over but keeps blockade in place
world.summary: President Donald Trump said Monday that the war with Iran was “militarily effectively over” after meeting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, but said the United States would maintain its naval blockade and keep forces ready to resume attacks. Trump said Gulf allies preferred the
world.content: President Donald Trump said Monday that the war with Iran was “militarily effectively over” after meeting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, but said the United States would maintain its naval blockade and keep forces ready to resume attacks. Trump said Gulf allies preferred the current position and described diplomacy as gaining momentum, but gave no details of an agreement. Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei rejected Washington’s account of negotiations as “imaginary talks.” Tehran has demanded an end to the blockade, sanctions relief, the release of frozen assets, compensation for war damage and an end to hostilities across the region; Iranian officials say they will not negotiate under pressure. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said negotiations had made little progress and a breakthrough was not imminent. The United States carried out limited strikes on Iran at least twice in the past week and disabled a ship it said was attempting to breach the blockade. Trump said Washington had identified 38 bridges as potential targets if attacks resume. A reported Qatari-mediated proposal remains under discussion, with no agreement on its terms.
world.image_alt: Trump calls Iran war effectively over but keeps blockade in place

world.title: Pope Leo draws 2.5 million in Buenos Aires, meets abuse survivors
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated an outdoor Mass for an estimated 2.5 million people in Buenos Aires on Nov. 9, the largest gathering of his papacy, during the first papal visit to Argentina in nearly four decades. Before the Mass, he visited a disability care home. He also continued urging President Javier Milei’s government t
world.content: Pope Leo XIV celebrated an outdoor Mass for an estimated 2.5 million people in Buenos Aires on Nov. 9, the largest gathering of his papacy, during the first papal visit to Argentina in nearly four decades. Before the Mass, he visited a disability care home. He also continued urging President Javier Milei’s government to protect vulnerable people affected by austerity measures. At the Pequeño Cottolengo Don Orione home in Claypole, which houses more than 400 people with disabilities, Leo said their lives were “a blessing, not a burden” and said a country’s progress should be judged in part by how it treats people with disabilities. The Argentine Congress overturned Milei’s veto of a disability-funding law last year, but his government has resisted implementing it, citing concerns about public finances. Leo also met privately with five people who said they had experienced abuse by clergy or in church institutions. The Vatican said he committed to strengthening protections. At a separate meeting with business and labor representatives, he defended unions’ role in protecting workers. His tour was scheduled to continue in Argentina on Tuesday before he travels to Peru; he is due back in Rome on Nov. 17.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo draws 2.5 million in Buenos Aires, meets abuse survivors

world.title: Steel plant blast in western Turkey kills 17 workers, prompts probe
world.summary: An explosion and fire at the HABAS iron and steel plant in Aliaga, western Turkey, killed 17 workers and injured at least 12 on Monday, Nov. 9, Turkish officials said. The death toll rose from 16 when a critically injured worker died, Health Minister Kemal Memisoglu said. Izmir Governor Suleyman Elban said an overhead
world.content: An explosion and fire at the HABAS iron and steel plant in Aliaga, western Turkey, killed 17 workers and injured at least 12 on Monday, Nov. 9, Turkish officials said. The death toll rose from 16 when a critically injured worker died, Health Minister Kemal Memisoglu said. Izmir Governor Suleyman Elban said an overhead crane collapsed into an electric arc furnace during boiler-replacement work. Officials said the impact damaged a gas line. Production had stopped for maintenance, leaving about 200 workers nearby rather than the usual 300. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said judicial and administrative inquiries would establish the cause and whether negligence was involved. Four public prosecutors were assigned to the investigation, and five people were reported detained. Workers’ groups called for accountability and announced a protest over workplace safety in Aliaga for Nov. 10.
world.image_alt: Steel plant blast in western Turkey kills 17 workers, prompts probe

world.title: UK court sentences comedian Russell Brand to 10½ years for rape, sexual assaults
world.summary: British comedian and actor Russell Brand was sentenced on Nov. 9 to 10 years and six months in prison for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. He is expected to serve two-thirds of the term in custody before release on licence and will face lifelong sex-offender notification requirements. A jury convi
world.content: British comedian and actor Russell Brand was sentenced on Nov. 9 to 10 years and six months in prison for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. He is expected to serve two-thirds of the term in custody before release on licence and will face lifelong sex-offender notification requirements. A jury convicted Brand on Nov. 5 after a four-week trial. He was acquitted of two other rape charges and a charge of attempted indecent assault. He had denied all the charges, maintaining that his sexual encounters were consensual. The convictions concerned offences between 2004 and 2009, including the rape of a 21-year-old fan and sexual assaults at a London bar, a radio station and a TV studio. Six women made allegations at trial; the court heard that four of them provided victim impact statements describing lasting trauma. London’s Metropolitan Police is investigating two further rape allegations against Brand, one involving a person who was 16 at the time. Police have appealed for victims to come forward. After sentencing, TV producer Jemima Goldsmith, Brand’s former partner, said he had subjected her to violence and coercive control. She said she called police during a 2014 incident but did not press charges.
world.image_alt: UK court sentences comedian Russell Brand to 10½ years for rape, sexual assaults

business.title: Rocket Lab sales beat forecasts, but Neutron delay weighs on shares
business.summary: Rocket Lab reported third-quarter sales of $268 million, up 73% from a year earlier and above analysts’ $257 million estimate, while its backlog reached $3.57 billion as of Sept. 30. Shares fell after the company also reported a $79.6 million net loss, wider than analysts expected, and pushed the first launch of its Ne
business.content: Rocket Lab reported third-quarter sales of $268 million, up 73% from a year earlier and above analysts’ $257 million estimate, while its backlog reached $3.57 billion as of Sept. 30. Shares fell after the company also reported a $79.6 million net loss, wider than analysts expected, and pushed the first launch of its Neutron rocket to no earlier than 2027. The delay followed the discovery in October of a manufacturing-process issue that left voids in part of a composite propellant-tank dome. Rocket Lab said it refined the process and is making a replacement component. For the fourth quarter, the company forecast revenue of up to $290 million but an adjusted loss of as much as $20 million, compared with the $10.9 million loss analysts expected.
business.image_alt: Rocket Lab sales beat forecasts, but Neutron delay weighs on shares

business.title: Iran war and renewables forecast to drive 0.4% drop in fossil-fuel emissions in 2026
business.summary: Global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are forecast to fall 0.4% in 2026, the first annual decline since 2020, according to the Global Carbon Budget assessment presented at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. Researchers attribute the drop partly to the Iran war and disruption to the Strait of Hormu
business.content: Global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are forecast to fall 0.4% in 2026, the first annual decline since 2020, according to the Global Carbon Budget assessment presented at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey. Researchers attribute the drop partly to the Iran war and disruption to the Strait of Hormuz, which drove up oil prices and reduced oil use, and partly to increased deployment of solar and wind power and electric vehicles. Despite the projected decline in fossil-fuel emissions, emissions from land-use change are forecast to push total CO2 emissions to 43.3 billion tonnes, up from 42.8 billion in 2025. Researchers estimate the remaining carbon budget for limiting warming to 1.5°C at about 150 billion tonnes—less than four years at current emission rates—and warn that emissions could rebound if oil tensions ease. They say faster deployment of clean-energy technologies is needed to sustain reductions.
business.image_alt: Iran war and renewables forecast to drive 0.4% drop in fossil-fuel emissions in 2026

business.title: Gold slips near $4,120 as investors await U.S. inflation data
business.summary: Gold prices eased on Tuesday after rising more than 1% in the previous session, with spot bullion trading around $4,115-$4,124 an ounce as investors awaited U.S. inflation figures. The Consumer Price Index report, due later Tuesday, may shift expectations for Federal Reserve policy. Traders put the chance of a December
business.content: Gold prices eased on Tuesday after rising more than 1% in the previous session, with spot bullion trading around $4,115-$4,124 an ounce as investors awaited U.S. inflation figures. The Consumer Price Index report, due later Tuesday, may shift expectations for Federal Reserve policy. Traders put the chance of a December rate increase at 84%, while Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin said the central bank should proceed “with care”. Lower oil prices, linked in part to hopes for U.S.-Iran diplomacy, had helped gold advance by easing inflation concerns, but higher interest rates can make non-yielding bullion less attractive than bonds. U.S. Producer Price Index data is due Friday.
business.image_alt: Gold slips near $4,120 as investors await U.S. inflation data

business.title: Medicare Advantage premiums set to fall, but coverage costs may rise
business.summary: Average monthly premiums for Medicare Advantage plans are expected to fall 16.5% in 2027, from $14.37 this year to $12, according to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services. But changes to copayments, deductibles and other benefits could leave some retirees paying hundreds or thousands of dollars more overall. N
business.content: Average monthly premiums for Medicare Advantage plans are expected to fall 16.5% in 2027, from $14.37 this year to $12, according to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services. But changes to copayments, deductibles and other benefits could leave some retirees paying hundreds or thousands of dollars more overall. Nearly 4.5 million people enrolled in Medicare Advantage plans with drug coverage are expected to need a new plan next year as insurers discontinue plans. Medicare’s open-enrollment deadline is Dec. 7, 2026; people whose coverage has been terminated have until Dec. 31 to enroll in a replacement plan.
business.image_alt: Medicare Advantage premiums set to fall, but coverage costs may rise

business.title: OCC grants Coinbase full national trust charter for custody
business.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency approved Coinbase National Trust Company’s full national trust charter on Nov. 6, bringing the crypto exchange’s institutional custody business under federal supervision. Coinbase announced the approval on Nov. 9. The charter permits fiduciary custody of digital assets for
business.content: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency approved Coinbase National Trust Company’s full national trust charter on Nov. 6, bringing the crypto exchange’s institutional custody business under federal supervision. Coinbase announced the approval on Nov. 9. The charter permits fiduciary custody of digital assets for clients but does not authorize retail deposits or conventional lending. Coinbase’s application outlines segregated custody accounts and plans to explore digital-asset payment products. Coinbase applied in October 2025 and received conditional approval in April 2026. The company said it spent the intervening months building compliance systems, hiring staff and completing regulatory reviews. Other crypto firms have sought federal trust charters, and the Independent Community Bankers of America has challenged the OCC’s authority to grant them.
business.image_alt: OCC grants Coinbase full national trust charter for custody

business.title: Philippine growth slows to 2.1%, putting 2026 target at risk
business.summary: The Philippine economy grew 2.1% year over year in the third quarter, slowing for the fifth consecutive quarter as weak household and government spending and falling farm output restrained activity. Growth averaged 2.5% in the first nine months, meaning the economy would need to expand 6.3% in the fourth quarter to rea
business.content: The Philippine economy grew 2.1% year over year in the third quarter, slowing for the fifth consecutive quarter as weak household and government spending and falling farm output restrained activity. Growth averaged 2.5% in the first nine months, meaning the economy would need to expand 6.3% in the fourth quarter to reach the lower end of its 3.5%-4.5% target for 2026, Economic Planning Secretary Arsenio Balisacan said. Inflation accelerated to 7.8% in October, while higher food and fuel costs and tighter financing conditions weighed on purchasing power and investment. The slowdown has prompted economists to urge the central bank to consider pausing rate increases, although Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Governor Eli Remolona Jr. said the bank remained in a tightening cycle to curb persistent price pressures. Balisacan said meeting the 2026 target would be “very challenging”; the government’s Development Budget Coordination Committee is due to revisit growth assumptions early next month. Officials say meeting the 2027 target of 5%-6% would require stronger investment, lower price pressures and restored business confidence.
business.image_alt: Philippine growth slows to 2.1%, putting 2026 target at risk

business.title: French supermarket refrigeration hack causes estimated losses of tens of millions of euros
business.summary: The October cyberattack forced French retailers to discard large quantities of fresh and frozen food. One supermarket chain reported losses of tens of millions of euros in a single day, while a store owner estimated nationwide costs could reach tens of millions. France has blamed Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corp
business.content: The October cyberattack forced French retailers to discard large quantities of fresh and frozen food. One supermarket chain reported losses of tens of millions of euros in a single day, while a store owner estimated nationwide costs could reach tens of millions. France has blamed Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps for remotely changing refrigeration settings at about 700 commercial sites, including supermarkets and smaller food businesses. Some affected refrigeration systems were obsolete or running outdated firmware, while France’s cybersecurity agency cited weak passwords and basic security gaps. The attack also started fires at affected sites. French authorities reported about 20 fires, while a separate French report cited at least 15. The Paris prosecutor’s office has opened an investigation and is seeking international arrest warrants. France says it will pursue European sanctions against those responsible.
business.image_alt: French supermarket refrigeration hack causes estimated losses of tens of millions of euros

business.title: California voters reject 5% billionaire tax aimed at healthcare funding
business.summary: California voters rejected Proposition 40, which would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of residents worth more than $1 billion. The measure lost 52.8% to 47.2%; supporters said it could raise about $100 billion, mainly for healthcare, with some money for education and food assistance. The proposal targeted
business.content: California voters rejected Proposition 40, which would have imposed a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of residents worth more than $1 billion. The measure lost 52.8% to 47.2%; supporters said it could raise about $100 billion, mainly for healthcare, with some money for education and food assistance. The proposal targeted residents’ wealth as of Jan. 1, 2026, and its backers presented it as a way to offset federal healthcare funding cuts. Opponents, including California Gov. Gavin Newsom, argued the tax could drive wealthy residents away and reduce the state’s income-tax revenue. Spending against the measure substantially exceeded spending in support: the Los Angeles Times reported that more than $400 million was spent across three linked ballot measures, with more than 90% of that spending directed against the billionaire tax. Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West President Dave Regan said the union would seek another tax proposal in 2028 if state lawmakers do not find a healthcare funding solution.
business.image_alt: California voters reject 5% billionaire tax aimed at healthcare funding

science.title: Stanford researchers use brain scans to flag Alzheimer’s risk years earlier
science.summary: Stanford Medicine researchers developed an MRI-based score that identified brain activity patterns linked to later cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease, potentially before memory problems or established biomarkers appear. The researchers developed the Alzheimer’s resilience-vulnerability connectome (ARC) score by
science.content: Stanford Medicine researchers developed an MRI-based score that identified brain activity patterns linked to later cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease, potentially before memory problems or established biomarkers appear. The researchers developed the Alzheimer’s resilience-vulnerability connectome (ARC) score by comparing brain scans taken at rest from 180 adults over 75 with unusually strong memory and 110 people diagnosed with Alzheimer’s. They then tested it in more than 1,300 cognitively healthy adults aged 55 to 70. During up to 12 years of follow-up, participants with more Alzheimer’s-like patterns experienced faster cognitive decline and were more likely to develop amyloid plaques or receive a diagnosis. The researchers say the score is neither a diagnosis nor a certain prediction for an individual. They are planning a trial to test whether cognitive training can change ARC scores.
science.image_alt: Stanford researchers use brain scans to flag Alzheimer’s risk years earlier

science.title: Delhi air quality forecast to remain severe for days
science.summary: Delhi’s air quality is forecast to stay in the “severe” category for several days after Diwali fireworks added smoke and fine particles to the capital’s seasonal pollution. During the annual winter smog, emissions from traffic, industry and crop-residue fires build up as weather conditions limit their dispersal. Reuter
science.content: Delhi’s air quality is forecast to stay in the “severe” category for several days after Diwali fireworks added smoke and fine particles to the capital’s seasonal pollution. During the annual winter smog, emissions from traffic, industry and crop-residue fires build up as weather conditions limit their dispersal. Reuters reported a citywide Air Quality Index (AQI) of 370 on Monday, while several local monitoring stations registered readings above 400, the threshold for “severe” on India’s scale. Delhi and the National Capital Region have implemented Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan. The air-quality early warning system forecast several days of severe conditions, with low winds and poor ventilation expected to keep pollutants concentrated. Delhi’s pollution action plan also called for schools to offer online classes.
science.image_alt: Delhi air quality forecast to remain severe for days

science.title: WMO warns strong El Niño could extend extreme weather into 2027
science.summary: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says the unusually strong 2026–27 El Niño is likely to bring additional heat and extreme weather through 2027. The pattern is forecast to peak in December or January, and the WMO says it could reach record strength in December. Global surface temperatures from January through
science.content: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says the unusually strong 2026–27 El Niño is likely to bring additional heat and extreme weather through 2027. The pattern is forecast to peak in December or January, and the WMO says it could reach record strength in December. Global surface temperatures from January through September 2026 averaged about 1.47°C above the preindustrial level, and the agency expects the year to rank among the warmest on record. Impacts will vary by region, with drought in some places and heavy rain or flooding in others. In the United States, forecasters expect a more typical El Niño weather pattern to emerge by late November; the winter outlook favors warmer conditions across much of the North and wetter conditions across parts of the South. Scientists caution that El Niño shifts the odds of weather patterns rather than directly causing individual storms. The U.S. National Weather Service said recent flooding in Florida and the Four Corners region could not yet be attributed to the pattern.
science.image_alt: WMO warns strong El Niño could extend extreme weather into 2027

science.title: NASA opens astronaut applications for lunar missions, sets Dec. 3 deadline
science.summary: NASA has opened applications for its 25th astronaut candidate class, seeking U.S. citizens to train for lunar surface missions and future work on a planned Moon base. Applications close Dec. 3, and NASA expects to announce its selections in late 2027. NASA is expanding its astronaut corps for Artemis lunar missions and
science.content: NASA has opened applications for its 25th astronaut candidate class, seeking U.S. citizens to train for lunar surface missions and future work on a planned Moon base. Applications close Dec. 3, and NASA expects to announce its selections in late 2027. NASA is expanding its astronaut corps for Artemis lunar missions and eventual crewed missions to Mars; the agency currently has 32 active astronauts. Applicants need qualifying advanced education and at least three years of relevant experience. Selected candidates are expected to begin training in early 2028. In the previous recruitment round, more than 8,000 people applied, and NASA selected 10 candidates in 2025.
science.image_alt: NASA opens astronaut applications for lunar missions, sets Dec. 3 deadline

science.title: Peruvian fossil reveals pygmy sperm whale with extreme skull asymmetry
science.summary: Researchers have described Scaphokogia huachafo, an extinct pygmy sperm whale whose fossil skull shows the most extreme facial asymmetry documented in a cetacean, and possibly in any mammal. The animal lived in what is now southern Peru between 6.3 million and 5.6 million years ago and was about 2.7 meters long. Both b
science.content: Researchers have described Scaphokogia huachafo, an extinct pygmy sperm whale whose fossil skull shows the most extreme facial asymmetry documented in a cetacean, and possibly in any mammal. The animal lived in what is now southern Peru between 6.3 million and 5.6 million years ago and was about 2.7 meters long. Both bony nostrils sat on the left side of its skull. Its dense, downward-curving snout and flexible neck suggest it searched for food in shallow seabed sediments. Researchers propose that it used echolocation to locate buried prey; unlike some bottom-feeding marine mammals, it had no facial whiskers or other specialized sensory structures for foraging.
science.image_alt: Peruvian fossil reveals pygmy sperm whale with extreme skull asymmetry

science.title: Voyager 1 to reach one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18
science.summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 is expected to reach one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, nearly 49 years after launch. At that distance—about 16.1 billion miles—a radio signal will take roughly 24 hours to travel each way, leaving mission controllers with about a two-day wait for a response. The spacecraft remains the most distant h
science.content: NASA’s Voyager 1 is expected to reach one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, nearly 49 years after launch. At that distance—about 16.1 billion miles—a radio signal will take roughly 24 hours to travel each way, leaving mission controllers with about a two-day wait for a response. The spacecraft remains the most distant human-made object and continues to send scientific data from interstellar space, which it entered in 2012. Its dwindling plutonium power supply has left only two instruments operating; NASA expects to lose contact with the probe around 2036. Scientists use its measurements of plasma and magnetic fields to study how far the Sun’s influence extends beyond the heliosphere.
science.image_alt: Voyager 1 to reach one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18

science.title: SpaceX targets first Starship double catch on November 13
science.summary: SpaceX plans to launch Starship Flight 15 from its Starbase site in Texas on Friday, November 13, and attempt to catch both rocket stages with the launch tower for the first time. The 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. Eastern, pending regulatory approval. SpaceX has caught the Super Heavy booster on three earl
science.content: SpaceX plans to launch Starship Flight 15 from its Starbase site in Texas on Friday, November 13, and attempt to catch both rocket stages with the launch tower for the first time. The 75-minute launch window opens at 5:45 p.m. Eastern, pending regulatory approval. SpaceX has caught the Super Heavy booster on three earlier flights but has never attempted to recover the Starship upper stage at the tower. The upper stage is expected to fly about 275 kilometers above Earth, completing roughly 14 orbits over more than 22 hours, deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites and then return for the planned catch. Flight controllers will proceed with the tower approach only if the spacecraft’s landing systems are ready; otherwise, SpaceX has planned ocean splashdown options. Flight 14, launched September 28, reached orbit for the first time but ended with a Pacific splashdown after an engine issue shortened the mission.
science.image_alt: SpaceX targets first Starship double catch on November 13

science.title: Researchers use living brain cells to power experimental computing systems
science.summary: Researchers are testing brain organoids—small models of brain tissue grown from stem cells—as computing systems, stimulating their neurons and translating their electrical activity into commands. Researchers discussed the work last month at the inaugural International Conference on Organoid Intelligence in Washington,
science.content: Researchers are testing brain organoids—small models of brain tissue grown from stem cells—as computing systems, stimulating their neurons and translating their electrical activity into commands. Researchers discussed the work last month at the inaugural International Conference on Organoid Intelligence in Washington, D.C. Scientists do not fully understand how neurons compute, and it can be difficult to determine whether the cells or the algorithms interpreting their activity are doing the work. Commercial devices and research demonstrations already exist, including a system that lets research teams run experiments remotely on organoids.
science.image_alt: Researchers use living brain cells to power experimental computing systems

sports.title: Eddie Howe rejects Crystal Palace role as Sage faces exit
sports.summary: Eddie Howe has rejected an approach to manage Crystal Palace, who are preparing to part with manager Pierre Sage after a poor start left the club bottom of the Premier League. Former Brentford and Tottenham manager Thomas Frank has emerged as Palace’s leading candidate, while Sean Dyche is also under consideration. Pal
sports.content: Eddie Howe has rejected an approach to manage Crystal Palace, who are preparing to part with manager Pierre Sage after a poor start left the club bottom of the Premier League. Former Brentford and Tottenham manager Thomas Frank has emerged as Palace’s leading candidate, while Sean Dyche is also under consideration. Palace have seven points from 10 league games and have conceded 24 goals; Sunday’s 3-1 home defeat by Liverpool was their fourth consecutive league loss. The club had considered a change as early as September but held off after a goalless draw at Leeds. After the November international break, Palace are scheduled to visit Coventry on November 21 and host Hull on November 29.
sports.image_alt: Eddie Howe rejects Crystal Palace role as Sage faces exit

sports.title: Ben White defends 2022 England exit before Nations League return
sports.summary: Arsenal defender Ben White says he would make the same decision to leave England’s 2022 World Cup camp and sit out selection under then-England manager Gareth Southgate, while declining to disclose what led to it. Back in England manager Thomas Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League, White says supporters do not know th
sports.content: Arsenal defender Ben White says he would make the same decision to leave England’s 2022 World Cup camp and sit out selection under then-England manager Gareth Southgate, while declining to disclose what led to it. Back in England manager Thomas Tuchel’s squad for the Nations League, White says supporters do not know the “full story” and that he will not blame anyone publicly. Some fans booed White when he returned against Uruguay in March. He then scored before conceding the penalty that led to a 1-1 draw. He missed this summer’s World Cup through injury and hopes to add to his six England caps in games against Croatia at Wembley on November 12 and Spain in Madrid on November 15.

sports.content: Arizona Cardinals receiver Michael Wilson will miss the rest of the season with a neck fracture, while quarterback Gardner Minshew is seeking additional medical opinions on a suspected ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) injury in his throwing arm that could require season-ending surgery. Both were injured in Arizona’s 17-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday. The 3-6 Cardinals face the Los Angeles Rams next without Wilson and with Minshew’s status uncertain. If Minshew cannot play, rookie Carson Beck is in line for his first regular-season NFL start on Sunday. Arizona has also signed veteran quarterback Josh Johnson from the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said the offense’s foundations would remain unchanged for Beck, who spent last week as the backup. Tests after the game revealed Wilson’s neck fracture; ESPN reported, citing a source, that he was expected to wear a brace for six weeks to two months.

sports.content: The R&A has selected Carnoustie Golf Links in Angus, Scotland, to host the 157th Open Championship in 2029, bringing golf’s oldest major back to the course for the first time since Francesco Molinari won there in 2018. Carnoustie will host the championship for the ninth time. The R&A says it worked with the venue on plans to improve the course and facilities ahead of the event. The Open is scheduled for St Andrews in 2027 and Royal Lytham in 2028 before returning to Carnoustie; the BBC lists the 2029 tournament dates as July 19-22. Scottish First Minister John Swinney said the tournament would bring tourism and jobs, while Carnoustie Golf Links says its investment aims to improve the course, facilities and visitor experience. Fans can register their interest in attending through The Open’s website.

sports.content: The NFL reinstated San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Monday, Nov. 9, after he reported for a physical, giving the team a two-game roster exemption through Nov. 23. The 49ers must decide whether to trade him, release him or add him to the active roster; the NFL trade deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. ET. Aiyuk, 28, has not played since tearing the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee on Oct. 20, 2024. He told reporters he feels healthy and wants to return, but San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan said reinstatement does not change the team’s plans and that Aiyuk’s time with the 49ers is over. San Francisco has not found a trade partner. The exemption gives the team until Nov. 23 to make a roster move if Aiyuk is not traded or released first.

sports.content: Tom Brady has ended his three-year involvement with Birmingham City, leaving the English second-tier club as it leads the Championship. The club announced his departure on Monday, Nov. 9, without giving a reason. Brady relinquished his minority stake, reported as 3.3%, and stepped down as chair of the club’s advisory board. Birmingham moved to the top after beating Swansea City 2-1 on Saturday and has 29 points from 15 matches. Brady joined in August 2023 through a partnership with Knighthead Capital Management. The club said he would invest and share his expertise, including advice on health, nutrition, wellness and recovery. During his tenure, Birmingham was relegated to League One in 2024, then won the third tier to return immediately to the Championship. Birmingham aims to return to the Premier League, and a top-two Championship finish would secure automatic promotion. The club’s long-term plans include a proposed 62,000-capacity stadium.

sports.content: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is expected to go on injured reserve after spraining the MCL and PCL in his right knee and suffering turf toe in Sunday’s 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders. Coach Sean McVay said the team expects Nacua to miss at least a month. Nacua was injured on a five-yard run on the Rams’ final offensive play. The 5-4 Rams are now without both of Matthew Stafford’s leading wide receivers: Davante Adams has been out since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 6. Nacua and Adams have combined for 100 of the team’s 120 receptions by wide receivers this season, leaving Los Angeles to rely more on its remaining receivers, tight ends and running backs. If placed on injured reserve, Nacua must miss at least four games. His first opportunity to return would be Dec. 20 against the Dallas Cowboys. Los Angeles plays at Arizona on Nov. 15, has a Week 11 bye, then faces Green Bay, Kansas City and San Francisco. McVay said the team would consider “all avenues” to address its receiving depth before Tuesday’s trade deadline.
